newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Oji Shinkin to merge with Musashino - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan Oji Shinkin to merge with Musashino - sources.

text.p: Oji Shinkin Bank will merge with financially troubled Musashino Shinkin Bank with support from other shinkin banks, industry sources said on Thursday.
Zenshinren Bank, a national association of credit associations, will provide 24.5 billion yen to help write off Musashino's bad loans, they also said.

Shinkin banks are small credit associations which take deposits and lend mainly to members and are supervised by the Ministry of Finance (MOF). The sources said the Tokyo Association of Shinkin Banks plans to set up a body to collect recoverable loans held by Musashino Shinkin.

Earlier on Thursday, the association said it would announce a plan to bail out Musashino Shinkin at a news conference starting at 4 p.m. (0700 GMT). By merging Musashino with a healthy shinkin bank with the all-out support of the shinkin banking sector, the sector is keen to prevent the failure from causing further unrest, analysts said.
